document.abstract: Broadcasters production and post facilities use a variety of public and private wide-area network technologies to connect remote studios to broadcast centers for voice, data and video communications services. By migrating all these services onto a single ATM infrastructure, a number of broadcasters production studios are now gaining significant operational and economic benefits. This paper describes how these integrated wide-area network services are deployed and provides details of the new TV networking services supported by an ATM infrastructure.
